description: Learning from data with the mathematics made explicit: regression, classification, trees and ensembles, neural networks trained by backpropagation, unsupervised learning, rigorous evaluation, feature engineering and the ethics of deployed models, with every algorithm implemented from scratch before using a library. Taught to the depth of a leading machine learning course.
modelledOn: Bishop, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning
Murphy, Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction
Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning (introductory chapters)
outcomes: Formulate supervised and unsupervised learning problems and derive and implement the core algorithms with gradient descent.
Fit and regularise linear and logistic regression models and interpret their coefficients.
Train decision trees, random forests and gradient-boosted ensembles and explain why ensembles work.
Implement a neural network with backpropagation and train it with modern optimisers and regularisation.
Evaluate models with appropriate metrics, cross-validation and learning curves and diagnose bias and variance.
Engineer features for tabular, text and image data and assess fairness, bias and privacy before deployment.

units.title: Supervised and unsupervised learning
topics: What learning from data means; supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised and reinforcement settings
Hypothesis spaces, loss functions, empirical risk minimisation; generalisation
Linear algebra, probability and calculus refresher as used in the course
Tooling: NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch; notebooks and experiment tracking

units.title: Linear regression
topics: Least squares: closed form and gradient descent; batch, stochastic and mini-batch
Feature scaling, polynomial features, basis functions
Ridge and lasso regularisation; the bias-variance trade-off
Probabilistic view: maximum likelihood with Gaussian noise; Bayesian regression in brief
Predicting crop yield or house prices in Accra from tabular data

units.title: Logistic regression and linear classifiers
topics: Logistic regression: sigmoid, cross-entropy loss, gradient, decision boundaries; multiclass with softmax
Generative versus discriminative: naive Bayes and Gaussian discriminant analysis
Support vector machines: margins, hinge loss, kernels
k-nearest neighbours and the curse of dimensionality

units.title: Model evaluation, overfitting and model selection
topics: Train, validation and test splits; k-fold and stratified cross-validation; data leakage
Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC and PR curves, AUC, log loss, RMSE, MAE; imbalanced classes
Bias and variance; learning curves; underfitting and overfitting diagnosis
Hyperparameter search: grid, random, Bayesian; nested cross-validation
Statistical significance of model comparisons; reporting results honestly

units.title: Decision trees and ensembles
topics: Decision trees: entropy, information gain, Gini, CART, pruning, handling continuous and missing values
Bagging and random forests; out-of-bag error; feature importance
Boosting: AdaBoost, gradient boosting, XGBoost and LightGBM; stacking
Why ensembles reduce variance; interpretability with SHAP and partial dependence

units.title: Neural networks and backpropagation
topics: Perceptron to multilayer perceptron; activation functions; universal approximation
Backpropagation derived and implemented with NumPy; computational graphs and automatic differentiation
Optimisation: SGD with momentum, Adam, learning-rate schedules; initialisation; batch normalisation
Regularisation: weight decay, dropout, early stopping, data augmentation
Convolutional networks for images and recurrent networks and transformers for sequences, in brief; transfer learning
Training a classifier for cassava leaf disease images

units.title: Unsupervised learning
topics: k-means, Gaussian mixture models and the EM algorithm; hierarchical and density-based clustering
Dimensionality reduction: PCA derived from variance maximisation and SVD; t-SNE and UMAP for visualisation
Anomaly detection; autoencoders in brief
Recommender systems: collaborative filtering and matrix factorisation

units.title: Feature engineering and the ML pipeline
topics: Encoding categorical variables, scaling, binning, interactions, date features, handling missing data
Text features: bag of words, TF-IDF, word embeddings; image features and pretrained encoders
Feature selection: filter, wrapper, embedded methods
Pipelines, reproducibility, model versioning and deployment basics (serving a model behind an API)

units.title: Learning theory and advanced topics
topics: PAC learning, VC dimension and generalisation bounds in brief
Online learning, active learning, semi-supervised learning
Reinforcement learning overview: bandits, Q-learning, policy gradients
Large language models and foundation models: what they are and how to use them responsibly

units.title: Ethics and bias in machine learning
topics: Sources of bias: data, labels, proxies, feedback loops; fairness definitions and their incompatibility
Explainability and accountability; model cards and datasheets
Privacy: differential privacy and federated learning in brief; data protection law
Case studies: credit scoring, facial recognition, predictive policing; deploying ML responsibly in Ghana
Capstone: a complete project with a model card and fairness audit

schedule.title: What learning from data means
schedule.exercise: Short problem set: classify five tasks as supervised, unsupervised or reinforcement, and compute the empirical risk of two hypotheses on a given dataset.

tasks.title: Load a small tabular dataset with pandas, split features and labels, and label each of five problem statements as supervised or unsupervised
Compute the empirical squared error of three candidate lines on a ten-point dataset and pick the best, then check it on held-out points
Set up a notebook that logs three experiments with parameters and metrics, rerun one with a fixed seed and show the results reproduce exactly

schedule.title: Linear regression
schedule.exercise: Derive the normal equations, solve a small example by hand, and compare closed form with gradient descent on a crop yield dataset.

tasks.title: Fit a line to 20 points with the closed-form least squares solution and with gradient descent and compare the coefficients
Fit polynomial regression of degree 1 to 12 with ridge and lasso penalties and plot validation error against complexity to show the bias-variance trade-off
Predict house prices in Accra from tabular features with feature scaling and regularisation, then report test RMSE against a mean baseline

schedule.title: Classifiers
schedule.exercise: Compare four classifiers on a small two-class dataset in a table of accuracy, training time and interpretability, and justify a choice.

tasks.title: Train a logistic regression on two features, plot its decision boundary and compute the probability for three new points
Train an SVM with linear and RBF kernels on non-separable data and show how the margin and boundary change with the C parameter
Evaluate k-nearest neighbours for dimension 2 to 100 on random data and show how accuracy and distances degrade with dimension

schedule.title: Evaluation and overfitting
schedule.exercise: Evaluate a spam classifier on an imbalanced dataset and write a short note on why accuracy alone misleads.

tasks.title: Split data into train, validation and test sets and run 5-fold cross-validation, reporting mean and spread of the accuracy
Compute precision, recall, F1 and AUC for a classifier on a 5 percent positive dataset and plot ROC and precision-recall curves
Plot learning curves for two models, diagnose which is underfitting and which is overfitting, and fix each, including one data leakage bug

schedule.title: Model selection and honest reporting
schedule.exercise: Write a results section comparing two models with a significance test and an honest statement of limitations.

tasks.title: Tune a model with grid search and random search at the same budget and compare the best scores found
Estimate generalisation error with nested cross-validation and show the plain cross-validation score is optimistic after tuning
Compare two classifiers over 10 cross-validation folds with a paired test and report effect size, confidence interval and whether the difference is real

schedule.title: Decision trees and forests
schedule.exercise: Build a decision tree by hand with information gain for a ten-row dataset and compare it with a random forest on a larger one.

tasks.title: Compute entropy and information gain for each candidate split on a ten-row dataset and step the tree growth one split at a time
Grow a decision tree with Gini impurity, then prune it by depth and plot training and test accuracy to find the best size
Train a random forest and report out-of-bag error, comparing it with a single tree and a bagged ensemble of 100 trees

schedule.title: Boosting and interpretation
schedule.exercise: Explain in a page why boosting reduces bias and bagging reduces variance, with a diagram.

tasks.title: Train a gradient boosting model for an increasing number of trees and plot the training and validation error for each
Compare random forest, gradient boosting and a stacked ensemble on the same tabular task and report accuracy, time and size
Explain a boosted model's predictions with permutation importance, partial dependence and SHAP values and say which features matter locally

schedule.title: Neural networks and backpropagation
schedule.exercise: Derive the gradients for a two-layer network by hand and check them numerically.

tasks.title: Step a perceptron through its updates on the AND and XOR data and observe which one it cannot learn
Implement a two-layer network and backpropagation in NumPy and verify each gradient against a finite difference check
Compare SGD, momentum and Adam with different learning rates and initialisations on the same network and plot the loss curves

schedule.title: Regularisation, CNNs and leaf diseases
schedule.exercise: Short report on the training choices you made for a leaf disease classifier and the evidence they helped.

tasks.title: Train a network on a small dataset with and without dropout, weight decay and early stopping, and compare validation accuracy
Fine-tune a pretrained convolutional model on a small image dataset and compare it with training the same architecture from scratch
Train a cassava leaf disease classifier with augmentation, report per-class precision and recall, and explain the confusions seen

schedule.title: Unsupervised learning
schedule.exercise: Cluster customer data of a mobile money agent with k-means and write what each cluster means for the business.

tasks.title: Run k-means with k from 2 to 8 on a two-dimensional dataset and use an elbow plot and silhouette score to pick k
Compute PCA from the covariance matrix of a small dataset, plot the principal axes and report the variance explained by each component
Build a matrix factorisation recommender on a ratings table, evaluate it with a held-out RMSE and describe how it behaves for new users

schedule.title: Features and pipelines
schedule.exercise: Write a reproducible pipeline specification for a loan default model, listing preprocessing, model, evaluation and deployment checks.

tasks.title: Encode categorical variables, scale numbers and impute missing values with a scikit-learn pipeline and check no test data leaks into fitting
Build TF-IDF features for 1,000 customer complaints and train a classifier to tag each complaint, then inspect the highest-weight words
Package a trained model in a versioned pipeline, serve it behind a small function call API and test it with malformed inputs

schedule.title: Theory and advanced topics
schedule.exercise: Short reflection: when would you choose reinforcement or active learning over supervised learning, and what are the risks of large language models?

tasks.title: Compute a PAC-style sample size bound for a finite hypothesis class and plot how it changes with the error and confidence parameters
Run Q-learning on a small gridworld for 500 episodes and watch the value table and learned policy change at each step
Compare random sampling with uncertainty-based active learning for labelling a pool of 1,000 examples and plot accuracy against labels used

schedule.title: Ethics, bias and the capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone deliverable: a complete project report with a model card, fairness audit and limitations section.

tasks.title: Measure demographic parity and equal opportunity of a credit scoring model for two groups and report the gap in each
Write a model card and datasheet for a classifier, filling in intended use, data sources, metrics by group and known failure cases
Complete an end-to-end project on an African dataset, run a fairness audit, mitigate the largest gap and report the effect on accuracy
